arxiv.title: Scale as a Modality: Multi-Scale Pixel-Space Diffusion Transformers
arxiv.star_quote: This design establishes the number of scales as a new architectural scaling dimension.
arxiv.headline: 空間スケールをモダリティとして扱うMS-pDiTによる高品質なピクセル空間拡散生成
arxiv.what: 空間スケールを独立したモダリティとして扱うマルチスケール・ピクセル空間拡散トランスフォーマーです。同一のノイズ画像を複数のパッチサイズでトークン化し、各スケール専用のストリームで処理しながら、MM-DiTスタイルの結合アテンションを通じて双方向に情報を交換します。
arxiv.enables: ImageNet 256x256において、スケール数を2から5に増やすことでFIDを4.39から2.19まで改善しました。また、ImageNet 512x512でFID 1.44、GenEvalで0.86を達成するなど、ピクセル空間での柔軟な生成が可能です。
arxiv.why_it_matters: 従来のLatent Diffusion Modelsが抱えていたオートエンコーダによる情報の損失や解像度の制約を回避し、スケール数を新たなスケーリング則として活用できる点に意義があります。

arxiv.title: TPS-A*: Path Planning for Any-Shape Vehicles with Certified Collision Checking in Trajectory Parameter Space
arxiv.star_quote: nearly sixty times faster than a state-lattice planner, the only other collision-free one
arxiv.headline: 軌道パラメータ空間での衝突判定により任意形状車両の高速なパスプランニングを実現するTPS-A*
arxiv.what: 任意の形状を持つ車両向けの格子状プランナー（Lattice Planner）であり、軌道パラメータ空間であらかじめ計算された衝突判定用グリッドを利用します。これにより、ノードごとの衝突判定コストが車両形状の複雑さや候補軌道数に依存しない仕組みを実現しています。
arxiv.enables: AMD Ryzen 7 2700X環境において、複雑な環境下でのクエリを中央値3ミリ秒で解決し、従来のState-Latticeプランナーと比較して約60倍の高速化を達成しました。非凸な形状の車両でも、衝突のない経路を保証しながらリアルタイムに計画可能です。
arxiv.why_it_matters: 安全性のための近似（円盤近似など）と計算コストのトレードオフを解消し、複雑な形状のロボットが狭い場所を高速かつ正確に移動できるようになります。

arxiv.title: FOSCAR: Accelerating Decode Attention over 2- and 4-Bit KV Caches through Affine Folding
arxiv.star_quote: FOSCAR increases peak aggregate throughput by up to 170% and 341% over 2-bit and 16-bit baselines, respectively.
arxiv.headline: 2/4ビット量子化KVキャッシュのデコード処理を高速化するカーネルライブラリFOSCAR
arxiv.what: LLMのデコード時におけるKVキャッシュのメモリアクセスを削減するため、Affine Foldingという手法を用いて量子化のスケールとオフセットの計算を最適化します。各KV値に個別に演算を適用するのではなく、行列演算の他方のオペランドや出力側に計算を寄せることで命令発行のボトルネックを解消します。
arxiv.enables: H100において、FlashInfer BF16比で最大3.36倍、TensorRT-LLM FP8比で最大2.03倍の高速化を達成しました。長文コンテキストの推論において、ピークスループットを最大170%から341%向上させることが可能です。
arxiv.why_it_matters: 量子化によるメモリ帯域の節約が必ずしも推論速度に直結しないという課題に対し、GPUのTensor CoreとALUの特性を考慮したハードウェアレベルの最適化を提供しています。

arxiv.title: CPU-ARC: Agentic Reasoning Caching for on-CPU Reasoning Reuse
arxiv.star_quote: ARCs show on-par performance with frontier LLMs across a range of difficult mathematical and scientific tasks, are fully explainable, continually trainable
arxiv.headline: LLMの推論プロセスをCPU実行可能な形式にキャッシュし再利用するCPU-ARC
arxiv.what: LLMが生成した推論トレースから、ロバストでCPU実行可能なAgentic Reasoning Caches (ARCs)を構築する手法です。一度解決したタスクの論理構造をキャッシュすることで、新しいインスタンスに対してLLMを介さずに効率的に解答を導き出します。
arxiv.enables: 科学的・数学的な難問において、フロンティアLLMと同等の性能を維持しつつ、推論コストを16倍から291倍削減しました。構築されたARCは完全に説明可能であり、継続的な学習も可能です。
arxiv.why_it_matters: LLMが似たような問題をゼロから解き直す非効率性を解消し、エッジデバイスや安価なCPU環境での高度な推論実行を可能にします。

arxiv.title: Energy-Based Reasoners: Your Recurrent Reasoner Should Be an Energy-Based Model
arxiv.star_quote: introduce Energy-Based Reasoners (EBRs), which learn an energy function over latent reasoning states
arxiv.headline: 再帰的推論をエネルギーベースモデルとして定式化するEnergy-Based Reasoners
arxiv.what: 潜在空間における反復的な推論プロセスを、エネルギー関数の勾配降下法として定式化するEnergy-Based Reasoners (EBRs)を提案しています。エネルギー関数が現在の推論状態の質をスコアリングし、その勾配が改善の方向をガイドします。
arxiv.enables: Sudoku-Extremeベンチマークにおいて、既存手法の345分の1の推論計算量で99.9%の精度を達成しました。また、複数の解が存在する問題において、高い多様性を保ちながらほぼ100%の正解率で解を生成できます。
arxiv.why_it_matters: 従来のループ構造を持つ推論モデルに「進捗の尺度」を導入し、効率的なステップ数での停止や、より正確な潜在状態への洗練を実現した点が重要です。
tags: エネルギーベースモデル

arxiv.title: Failure Profiling and Reachable Trajectory Selection for Reasoning Distillation
arxiv.comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026. The source code and trained weights are available at \url{https://github.com/visresearch/FPRT}
arxiv.star_quote: Experiments demonstrate that our method achieves the SOTA performance across the five benchmarks
arxiv.headline: 生徒モデルの失敗を分析し再現可能な推論ステップを選択して学習させるFPRT
arxiv.what: 教師モデルの推論を蒸留する際、生徒モデルが「何に失敗し、何を現実的に学習可能か」に基づいてデータを構成するFailure Profiling and Reachable Trajectory Selection (FPRT)を提案しています。失敗モードに応じてプロンプトを使い分け、生徒が再現しやすい修正ステップを持つ推論軌跡を選択します。
arxiv.enables: 5つのベンチマークにおいて、複数のモデルでSOTA性能を達成しました。特に推論の転換点（分岐点）における生徒モデルの再現性を重視することで、教師モデルへの過学習を防ぎ、推論能力の汎化を向上させています。
arxiv.why_it_matters: 教師モデルの出力をそのまま模倣させるのではなく、生徒モデルの現在の能力水準に合わせた最適な学習データを選定することで、蒸留効率を高めるアプローチです。

hf.title: From Autonomous Agents to Cognitive Symbionts: Toward AI-Augmented Human Intelligence
hf.abstract: For a decade, progress in artificial intelligence has been measured by how much a machine can do on its own. Large foundation models now write code and run multistep tasks, and personal agents act on a person's behalf. Yet people still forget what they once knew, miss what they are not looking at, fail to find the right words, and face hard choices without the benefit of their own history, because the machine that could help stands outside the situation. As AI moves into the physical world, attention has settled on one kind of intelligent individual, the embodied robot; we argue that the era of Physical AI holds a second kind of equal importance, the person augmented by AI. Alongside artificial general intelligence, which asks how intelligent a machine can be, stands AI-augmented human intelligence (AHI), which asks how much intelligence a machine can enable in a particular person. Realizing it calls for a new kind of system, a cognitive symbiont: a lifelong, embedded, real-time, private, low-friction, and proactive companion that senses what the person senses through external devices, keeps their context across years, models their situation and their mind, takes part in their thinking at the right moment, carries out everyday tasks with their context, and keeps learning the person as both change. We give the paradigm a conceptual core, the cognitive gap between what a person could bring to a situation and what they can hold in working memory, and organize its design space as a symbiosis loop of sensing, keeping, understanding, living alongside, acting for and thinking with the person, and growing, enclosed by a personal runtime and by trust. Because a symbiont changes what a person can do in front of others, it also raises risks of a new kind, from covert assistance in examinations to pressure on everyone to adopt it, and we treat their governance as part of the paradigm.
hf.title_ja: 自律型エージェントから認知共生体へ：AIによる人間知能の拡張に向けて
hf.summary_ja: AIを外部の道具ではなく、人間の認知を身体的・精神的に補完する「共生体」と定義し、AI拡張型人間という新たな方向性を提案する。

hf.title: VFlash: Fast, Accurate Visual Planning via Flash Primitive Decoding
hf.abstract: Models for physical AI tasks, such as robotics and autonomous driving, need not reason solely in language. They can use visual plans--points, bounding boxes, and trajectories--to represent spatial goals and anticipate motion. However, autoregressive vision-language models generate these plans one coordinate token at a time, making richer predictions increasingly costly. We introduce VFlash, a method for fast, accurate visual planning through Flash Primitive Decoding. VFlash exploits the known structure of visual primitives to predict their coordinates jointly, using a lightweight drafter that generates an entire primitive in one forward pass. The layout adapts to the primitive's type, dimensionality, and length, supporting compact boxes and long, variable-length trajectories. Crucially, spatial accuracy need not require reproducing an autoregressive model's exact token sequence. VFlash therefore trains on annotated primitives and directly accepts structurally valid predictions without target-token agreement. Across the evaluated 2D and 3D robot trajectory tasks, VFlash consistently reduces prediction errors relative to autoregressive decoding. Preliminary single-rollout measurements indicate approximately 25x faster generation for 3D point motion forecasting. A world action model conditioned on VFlash plans achieves 70.2% average success across four MolmoSpaces task suites, compared with 62.6% for the baseline.
hf.title_ja: VFlash：Flash Primitive Decodingによる高速かつ正確な視覚プランニング
hf.summary_ja: 座標を1つずつ生成する代わりに、視覚プリミティブの構造を利用して一括予測することで、ロボット等の視覚計画を高速化・高精度化する。

hf.title: SLA: Scaling Spatial-Language-Action Model via Continual Pre-training
hf.abstract: Reliable robotic manipulation requires both semantic understanding and precise control in three-dimensional space. However, vision-language-action (VLA) foundations largely inherit visual representations from 2D vision-language pre-training, while spatial supervision is often introduced only during task-specific adaptation. Developing spatial understanding as a transferable foundation-model capability therefore calls for learning from broader robot experience. We present SLA, a Spatial-Language-Action Model that scales implicit spatial alignment to continual pre-training and maintains it during downstream post-training. Initialized from a pretrained pi05 policy, SLA jointly optimizes action prediction and alignment between intermediate visual embeddings and spatial representations from a frozen 3D perception model. We curate and unify heterogeneous robot datasets to support spatial learning across diverse embodiments, tasks, and scenes. To accommodate this diversity, we introduce feature-dependent gates that adaptively aggregate visual embeddings from multiple VLA layers for spatial supervision. The teacher further exploits partially available depth and camera calibration alongside RGB observations, enabling effective use of heterogeneous geometric annotations. Probabilistic state dropout encourages reliance on visual cues and mitigates overfitting to demonstration trajectories. All auxiliary components are used only during training, allowing direct reuse of pretrained VLA weights and preserving the original inference architecture.
hf.title_ja: SLA：継続事前学習による空間・言語・行動モデルのスケールアップ
hf.summary_ja: 2D表現に依存しがちなVLAモデルに対し、継続事前学習を通じて暗黙的な空間アライメントを導入し、ロボット操作の精度を向上させる。

hf.title: Route Anything: A Study of Model and Policy Routing for General-Purpose AI Systems
hf.abstract: Artificial general intelligence (AGI) requires a method that can understand, generate, reason, and act across diverse domains and modalities. Rather than relying on a single model to master every capability, a promising path toward AGI now is to orchestrate a heterogeneous ecosystem of specialized models, tools, and policies (candidates) into a unified AI system. At the heart of this vision lies a fundamental question: how can an AI system dynamically select and coordinate the most capable candidate for each task while balancing performance and computational cost? In this work, we present Route Anything, a unified framework for studying model and policy routing across general-purpose AI systems. We develop a unified theoretical foundation that characterizes optimal routing under quality--cost trade-offs and establishes how the information available to a router determines its attainable performance. To systematically investigate routing across diverse capabilities, we first construct an omni-modal trajectory matrix spanning 25 benchmarks across language understanding, image, video, and speech generation, coding and workplace agents, and robotic manipulation, comprising 374,401 scored runs from 452 candidate configurations. Building on this framework, we train and test different routers to investigate the potential of omni-modal model routing, the capabilities of learned routers, and the conditions under which routing improves efficiency. Our results reveal substantial opportunities for capability orchestration: per-input oracle routing outperforms the best fixed candidate by 5.4 points, and learned routers outperform it by 0.3 points across 16 benchmarks, by 2.1 points on video generation, and by 1.1 points on robot manipulation while using 24% less policy time. More importantly, routing raises efficiency by 8.82x on average compared with the reference model.
hf.title_ja: Route Anything：汎用AIシステムにおけるモデルとポリシーのルーティング研究
hf.summary_ja: 単一モデルに頼らず、多様な専門モデルやツールから各タスクに最適な候補を動的に選択・調整するための統一フレームワークを提案。

hf.title: Behind Video Generation: Observations and Insights on Multimodal Understanding from Kling
hf.abstract: Video generation has progressed from isolated clips to coherent short-form audiovisual sequences, and the bottleneck is shifting from rendering to semantic control. This report summarizes the observations and insights on multimodal understanding gained from successive generations of Kling. We argue that generation quality is the projection of multimodal understanding through the entire data--conditioning--alignment--evaluation chain, and we examine this chain module by module. Kling-MLLM, a shared multimodal foundation model that unifies image, video, audio, synchronized audio--video, and interleaved inputs, is specialized for each downstream module. Because a DiT is trained on far fewer training samples than a language model, we treat captioning as a semantic contract that maximizes description density, and extend it to reference-grounded captioning that makes reference bindings explicit. Prompt enhancement translates user intent into this caption distribution: basic PE is derived from captions of compelling videos and refined with text-level and generator-in-the-loop reinforcement learning, while agentic PE refines the story and retrieves compelling examples. We show that a reliable text encoder comes from perceptual training rather than from stronger language ability, and that candidates can be screened from text alone before end-to-end training. Reward modeling pairs a general reward model for explainable, localized critiques with a decision reward model for fast multidimensional scoring, treating perceptual bandwidth as a first-class design parameter. Finally, we review task-specific automatic evaluation, focusing on protocols that expose scoring shortcuts and help trace failures to their upstream source. We hope these lessons offer practical guidance for building the understanding stack behind controllable video generation.
hf.title_ja: 動画生成の裏側：Klingから得られたマルチモーダル理解の知見と洞察
hf.summary_ja: 動画生成モデルKlingの開発を通じ、生成品質はデータから評価までの一連のチェーンにおけるマルチモーダル理解の投影であることを解説。

hf.title: Words Caught in the Heart: Simulating Person-Specific Expression for Self-Opaque Clients in Psychotherapy
hf.abstract: Psychotherapy clients may experience distress before they can coherently describe it, and their expression changes with emotion, perceived safety, and trust. Large language model-based client simulators often rely on clinically organized case descriptions, which can encourage responses explaining the client's difficulties more clearly than their current understanding warrants. We propose Pandora, a psychotherapy client simulation framework that models how psychological experience becomes situated, individual expression. Pandora updates psychological and relational states in response to therapist interventions, constructs subjective appraisals and attributions, and plans response content and strategy. A separate expression planner combines these decisions with language patterns distilled from the client's utterances to guide linguistic realization. We evaluate Pandora against five baselines on 115 cases from four counseling and motivational interviewing datasets. It achieves the highest expression similarity and overall disclosure-alignment score among the compared systems. In a four-evaluator study of 45 matched disclosure items, Pandora receives AI-like judgments in 7.2% of ratings, compared with 43.3--67.2% for the baselines and 35.6% without expression planning. The ablation also reduces expression similarity. These results support explicit expression planning in client simulation to improve alignment with individual language patterns and reduce perceived AI-like expression in the evaluated setting.
hf.title_ja: 心に捕らわれた言葉：心理療法における自己不透明なクライアントの表現シミュレーション
hf.summary_ja: 自身の問題を説明できない患者を模し、セラピストとの関係や心理状態に応じて主観的な反応を生成する心理療法シミュレーターPandoraを提案。

hf.title: MoviEdit: Long-form Multi-Shot Video Editing Made Easy
hf.abstract: Long-form multi-shot video editing requires an intended edit to remain coherent across abrupt changes in scene, viewpoint, and subject appearance, while processing substantially longer visual context than conventional single-shot editors. We introduce MoviEdit, an end-to-end framework for scalable long-form multi-shot video editing that jointly addresses the challenges of data, modeling, and evaluation. To provide cross-shot supervision data at scale, we develop automatic data-generation pipelines spanning synchronized multi-view footage, real-world multi-shot videos, and generated multi-shot content, yielding 87K paired editing videos without manual annotation. Architecturally, MoviEdit employs a cascaded bidirectional-autoregressive design: a lightweight bidirectional stage first establishes a globally coherent editing draft over a spatiotemporally compressed representation, which is then autoregressively propagated and refined over the full video. We further introduce MoviEdit-Bench, a dedicated benchmark for systematic evaluation of long-form multi-shot video editing. Extensive experiments show that MoviEdit substantially outperforms existing open-source models and performs on par with industry frontier models across text-guided and image-guided editing. Visit our project page for complete results and to access the benchmark: https://multi-shot-edit.github.io/
hf.title_ja: MoviEdit：長尺マルチショット動画編集の容易化
hf.summary_ja: シーンや視点が切り替わる長尺動画において、一貫性を保ちながら編集を可能にする自動データ生成パイプラインとエンドツーエンドのフレームワーク。

hf.title: Harness-S: Learning from Sibling Harnesses for Generalizable Agent Training
hf.abstract: Harness evolution from a common base exhibits Locality, Complementarity, and Nonstationarity: variants repair different failures, and their utility changes as the policy learns. Rather than seeking a universally superior harness, we introduce Harness-S to selectively rescue failures of a base execution system through sibling harnesses and transfer the resulting capabilities into a single policy that remains effective under the original harness. Directional Harness Evolution develops specialized sibling harnesses along distinct repair directions, forming a reusable Sibling Harness Pool that remains fixed during policy training. Complementary Harness Rescue Training invokes this pool only when all initial attempts under the base harness fail. The same policy generates fresh rollouts under selected auxiliary harnesses, and these trajectories replace the failed group for reinforcement learning. An Adaptive Harness Router selects the Top-k variants using Harness Behavior Profiles and voting across multiple LLMs. Policy-aware profile re-anchoring refreshes this evidence as the policy learns. Across AppWorld, SWE-Gym, and DBBench, the trained policy substantially outperforms policy-only training when returned to the original base harness. Behavioral analyses and held-out cases support the transfer of harness-elicited behaviors into the policy itself. Reusing the router for Rank-1 inference provides additional gains at the same executor rollout count.
hf.title_ja: Harness-S：汎用エージェント学習のための兄弟ハーネスからの学習
hf.summary_ja: 特定の失敗を救済する複数の補助的な実行環境（兄弟ハーネス）を活用し、単一のポリシーであらゆる失敗を克服できるように訓練する手法。

hf.title: SplatAnything: Gaussian Spacing Normalization for Feed-forward 3DGS across Arbitrary Scenes
hf.abstract: We identify a key limitation of existing feed-forward 3DGS methods: Gaussian attributes are typically predicted in a radial-distance-normalized space that canonicalizes a global radial statistic of the reconstructed geometry, while the spacing between neighboring Gaussian centers can still vary substantially across scene scales and camera configurations. This mismatch induces systematic shifts in Gaussian-scale targets, leading to ambiguous supervision. To address this, we propose SplatAnything with Gaussian Spacing Normalization (GSNorm), which canonicalizes a robust scene-level statistic of Gaussian spacing to provide a more consistent spatial reference for Gaussian prediction. To rigorously assess our method, we further establish a systematic benchmark spanning diverse datasets, input sparsity levels, and challenging extrapolated viewpoints. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SplatAnything achieves state-of-the-art performance, with particularly strong gains under substantial variations in scene scale and viewpoint.
hf.title_ja: SplatAnything：任意のシーンに対応する3DGSのためのガウス間隔正規化
hf.summary_ja: シーンのスケールによる予測の曖昧さを解消するため、ガウス間の間隔を正規化するGSNormを導入し、高精度な3Dガウススプラッティングを実現。

hf.title: Think Less, Locally: Local Preference Learning for Reasoning Compression
hf.abstract: Large reasoning models achieve strong performance on challenging tasks, but their long chain-of-thought often incurs substantial inference costs by continuing to deliberate after sufficient information has been obtained. Existing reasoning compression methods primarily operate on reasoning trajectories, paying less attention to the local decision of whether further reasoning is necessary given the current state. We propose LoCo, a local preference learning method for reasoning compression. LoCo detects candidate overthinking states from the model's own traces, freezes the corresponding reasoning prefixes, regenerates shorter verified continuations from the same states, and trains on the resulting state-conditioned preference pairs with DPO. This formulation teaches the model when to continue reasoning and when to conclude, rather than simply encouraging shorter trajectories overall. We construct training data entirely from self-generated mathematical traces and evaluate LoCo on five mathematical and three code generation benchmarks. LoCo reduces completion length by 41.7\%--45.4\% on mathematics and 23.4\%--36.3\% on code, while maintaining or improving accuracy and achieving the best AUC across all code benchmarks. LoCo consistently improves the accuracy-efficiency trade-off on mathematics and transfers effectively to code generation despite math-only training, demonstrating the cross-domain generality of local preference learning for reasoning compression. The code and model will be publicly released at https://github.com/MuyaoYuan/LoCo.
hf.title_ja: 思考を減らし、局所的に：推論圧縮のための局所的嗜好学習
hf.summary_ja: 思考の連鎖における「考えすぎ」の状態を検出し、情報の十分な地点で推論を切り上げることで、性能を維持しつつ推論コストを削減するLoCoを提案。

hf.title: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research
hf.abstract: AI agents are playing an increasingly important role in physics research. However, existing physics benchmarks only evaluate fixed questions, isolated sub-tasks, or paper reproduction with given solutions, and rarely check research quality alongside correctness. We introduce FrontierPhysics, an end-to-end benchmark with 56 tasks made by 42 physicists based on their own research, covering nine domains across theoretical, computational, and experimental physics. Each task requires agents to review the literature, develop a research plan, conduct research and experiments, and produce structured outputs and scientific manuscripts. Combining deterministic verifiers with expert-authored rubrics, FrontierPhysics evaluates whether agents' research is correct and publishable. Across 22 models in 26 configurations, no configuration passes more than 46 of its 168 rollouts. Manual review of agent trajectories shows that frontier agents' main weaknesses are insufficiently rigorous reasoning and limited expert intuition, rather than gaps in physics knowledge or execution errors.
hf.title_ja: FrontierPhysics：エンドツーエンドの物理研究用エージェントの評価
hf.summary_ja: 文献調査から実験、論文執筆まで、物理学の9領域にわたる研究の質と正確性を専門家基準で評価する新しいベンチマークを構築。

hf.title: From Pixels to Actions - Towards Native Vision-Language-Action Policies
hf.abstract: Vision-language-action models are typically built on a simple premise: perception is first compressed by visual encoders, and action reasoning begins only afterwards. Yet manipulation often hinges on precisely the visual signals most vulnerable to this abstraction, e.g., local geometry, boundaries, depth, and subtle state changes. This raises a fundamental question: should action policies inherit a fixed visual endpoint, or directly access evolving visual computation? We introduce NEO-VLA, a structurally encoder-free vision-language-action framework. Images are tokenized by lightweight patch convolutional layers and evolve jointly with language throughout the backbone, allowing a flow-matching action expert to draw from instruction-conditioned visual representations at different depths. This simple change reveals a consistent pattern. Native architectures outperform encoder-based counterparts under controlled comparisons; full fine-tuning reduces but does not erase the gap, and additional scale alone cannot recover it. More strikingly, layer-wise probing shows that the action-critical signals often peak well before the final visual representation. Across diverse manipulation settings and distribution shifts, NEO-VLA consequently achieves stronger and more robust control. Together, these results suggest that embodied control benefits from access to visual representations across the computational hierarchy, rather than a fixed encoder output.
hf.title_ja: ピクセルから行動へ：ネイティブな視覚・言語・行動ポリシーに向けて
hf.summary_ja: 視覚エンコーダを排除し、画像トークンと言語がバックボーン内で共に進化することで、細かな幾何学情報を直接行動に反映させるNEO-VLAを提案。

hf.title: DreamX: Video Diffusion Model is a Universal Latent Action Learner
hf.abstract: Learning a universal action representation from video requires modeling dynamics that are consistent across different executions of the same action yet invariant to changes in embodiment and appearance. Existing latent action models infer actions from visual transitions, but their representations often entangle the underlying action with irrelevant visual variations, limiting transfer across embodiments. We introduce DreamX, which repurposes a pretrained video diffusion model as a universal latent action learner. Our approach extracts compact latent actions from the video model's rich spatiotemporal features, compressing each latent video frame by 300times (1{,200 rightarrow 4} tokens). In addition, by leveraging the video model's generative prior, these latent actions capture action-relevant dynamics disentangled from visual appearance. The resulting latent space serves as a shared action interface across embodiments (human and robot), environments, and action parameterizations. On LARY-Bench, DreamX achieves state-of-the-art performance among latent action models. Moreover, actions encoded in one setting remain effective in another: the latent space supports any-to-any video transfer and zero-shot action transfer across diverse embodiments and environments. Furthermore, this shared interface also enables policy learning in a compact latent action space, reducing the computational cost of video-diffusion-based policies.
hf.title_ja: DreamX：動画拡散モデルは普遍的な潜在行動学習器である
hf.summary_ja: 訓練済みの動画拡散モデルから、見た目や実施形態に依存しない普遍的な潜在行動表現を抽出し、ロボット操作の学習に活用するDreamXを提案。

hf.title: Confucius4-R2T2: A Stable-Prefix Streaming ASR Model for Real Real-Time Transcription
hf.abstract: Streaming speech recognition is increasingly consumed by machines, such as translators and voice agents, that act on each token as it appears. A token that is later revised costs wasted work or a wrong action. In this work, we present Confucius4-R2T2 (short for Real Real-Time Transcription), a stable-prefix streaming ASR model that never modifies its earlier output while maintaining high accuracy and low latency. R2T2 is obtained by post-training Qwen3-ASR-1.7B on 1,500 hours of Chinese and English audio while freezing its pre-trained audio encoder and projector. The adaptation is based on the concept of Longest Stable Prefix (LSP), a new notion that we introduce in this work. We prove that LSP is monotone under the prefix order, consistent with the full-audio output, and maximal among labels that equal a whole earlier output. Learning from LSP labels converts a full-context model into a stable-prefix streaming one without any architectural change. Extensive evaluations show that R2T2 brings streaming recognition close to the base model's full-context quality while delivering stable text with low emission lag. Its gains extend beyond the post-training languages, demonstrating a practical path from full-context ASR to stable streaming. We open-source the model weights and code at https://huggingface.co/netease-youdao/Confucius4-R2T2 and https://github.com/netease-youdao/Confucius4-R2T2.
hf.title_ja: Confucius4-R2T2：真のリアルタイム文字起こしのための安定プレフィックス型ストリーミングASRモデル
hf.summary_ja: 一度出力した文字を後から修正しない「安定プレフィックス」特性を持ち、高精度かつ低遅延で機械処理に適した音声認識モデルを実現。

hf.title: Random Is Almost Enough? Stable and Low-Cost Benchmark Compression via BestRand
hf.abstract: Benchmark compression reduces the often prohibitive time and cost of model evaluation by evaluating models on a small benchmark subset that closely matches full-benchmark results. To quantify estimation error, we derive an accurate analytical approximation to the error distribution when estimating full-benchmark scores from a subset, showing that most subsets yield small errors, while a few produce much larger errors, resulting in a long-tailed distribution. This means random sampling alone can achieve surprisingly strong performance with high probability, but remains unstable due to rare large errors. We further show that this instability is inherent to modern foundation models and persists even as more models are evaluated. Based on these findings, we introduce BestRand, a stable and low-cost benchmark compression method that preserves the efficiency of random sampling while substantially reducing its high-error tail. We validate BestRand on 70+ text, multimodal, and agent benchmarks, and further extend it to VLA evaluation. Compared with competitive methods, BestRand reduces high-error risk by 50.2% and estimation error by 16.4% on average, while requiring only 51.3% of the construction cost. It further reduces OOD estimation error by 21.8% on average across score-range, model-family, and temporal shifts. Together, our theory provides practical guidance for understanding and predicting the accuracy and reliability of benchmark compression, while BestRand enables stable and accurate compression at low cost. The code and data are publicly available onhttps://github.com/George-Ling3/BestRand.
hf.title_ja: ランダムで十分か？BestRandによる安定・低コストなベンチマーク圧縮
hf.summary_ja: 少数の評価用データを選別する際、ランダム抽出の誤差分布を分析し、不安定さを解消して全データ評価の結果を高い信頼性で近似する手法を提示。

hf.title: Turns Matter: Advancing Streaming Video RL via Turn-Level Credit
hf.abstract: Streaming video understanding requires models to repeatedly decide whether to respond or continue observing. Recently, Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) has been applied to this setting, with existing approaches emphasizing reward design while retaining a single trajectory-level advantage across turns. Such shared credit can reinforce redundant replies after earlier successes and discourage useful follow-ups after earlier failures. We propose TurnWise, a turn-level GRPO framework that aligns learning with individual streaming decisions. TurnWise addresses the mismatch between trajectory-level feedback and turn-level interaction, promoting informative responses and reducing redundancy. Specifically, turn-level credit assignment uses silence-completed prefix scoring to construct group-relative advantages from each decision's remaining return, separating its learning signal from earlier rewards. Turn-mean policy optimization averages token losses within each turn and then across turns, giving response and waiting decisions equal weight regardless of output length. These complementary designs improve streaming policy learning without a learned critic or additional rollouts. Extensive experiments show our method outperforms prior RL approaches for streaming video understanding.
hf.title_ja: ターンが重要：ターンレベルの報酬割当によるストリーミング動画強化学習の進化
hf.summary_ja: 動画視聴中の応答判断において、一連の流れではなく各発話（ターン）単位で報酬を割り当てることで、冗長な応答を減らし適切な対話を促進する。

hf.title: RoboColosseum: Evaluating Physical Intelligence at Scale In-The-Wild
hf.abstract: General-purpose robot policies must work across robots, tasks, and environments, yet the variation that makes physical trials informative also makes them difficult to reproduce. We introduce RoboColosseum, a distributed evaluation framework that combines unified policy serving and standardized protocols across a network of locally operated robots in diverse environments. Our initial study evaluates five vision-language-action (VLA) policies and three frontier AI agents across four embodiments (SO-101, Franka, Bimanual-YAM, and G1 Humanoid). The Open Track compares models without task-specific adaptation in blinded, pairwise trials under matched local conditions. The Fine-tune Track measures how well VLA policies adapt to 20 tasks across all four embodiments when each policy receives the same 100 demonstrations per task. Across 5,699 pairwise Open Track comparisons at 124 sites, frontier agents rival specialized VLA policies, while all systems struggle to complete open-world tasks reliably. After fine-tuning, GR00T N1.7 leads on SO-101 and pi0.5 leads on Franka and Bimanual-YAM. Policy rankings show weak agreement across embodiment-specific task suites (Kendall W = 0.24). Open Track rankings poorly predict relative performance after fine-tuning, with substantial rank reversals on all three embodiments shared between tracks. Measuring partial progress reveals differences that task success alone misses. On the G1 Humanoid, no policy completes any of the five tasks, yet average progress ranges from 13.3% to 23.2% across policies. Open Track rankings stabilize as trials accumulate, and active matchmaking achieves comparable ranking agreement with substantially fewer physical trials than uniform sampling. These results show how distributed physical evaluation can reveal where robot policies generalize, how well they adapt to new tasks, and how far they progress on tasks they fail to complete.
hf.title_ja: RoboColosseum：野生環境における物理的知能の大規模評価
hf.summary_ja: 異なる場所にある様々なロボットや環境をネットワークで繋ぎ、統一プロトコルでVLAモデル等の性能を実戦形式で評価する分散型フレームワーク。

hf.title: Axion 1.0: Open Agent Foundation Models, Simplified
hf.abstract: We introduce Axion 1.0, a fully open agent foundation model that combines strong and broad agentic capabilities with a remarkably simple training recipe. Axion 1.0 is trained in only three stages: two lightweight supervised fine-tuning stages followed by reinforcement learning, without dedicated mid-training, direct preference optimization (DPO), or on-policy distillation (OPD). The first SFT stage develops strong self-contained reasoning through model-aware data construction, where we synthesize challenging problems and adversarially strengthen them based on the base model's own successful solution strategies. The second stage extends these capabilities to tool-dependent reasoning through a scalable pipeline for constructing diverse and automatically verifiable tasks grounded in real-world data sources and deterministic computation. Finally, reinforcement learning further strengthens long-horizon reasoning and interaction with external tools and environments. Despite this compact training recipe, Axion 1.0 achieves strong performance across a broad suite of agentic benchmarks and is competitive with leading commercial models on several of them. Equally importantly, Axion 1.0 is open beyond model weights: we release the complete recipe, including data construction, generation, filtering, verification, prompts, and training code, enabling the entire development process to be reproduced and extended. Axion 1.0 demonstrates that strong agent foundation models can be both open and simple, offering a practical and reproducible path toward advancing open agentic intelligence.
hf.title_ja: Axion 1.0：簡素化されたオープンなエージェント基盤モデル
hf.summary_ja: 複雑な中間学習を省き、自己構築データによるSFTと強化学習のみで、推論やツール利用に優れた高い能力を持つ完全オープンなモデルを開発。

hf.title: WeLM-Image: A Unified Image Generation Model towards Visual Intelligence
hf.abstract: We present WeLM-Image, a unified image foundation model that integrates multimodal understanding into text-to-image generation, instruction-guided editing, and multi-reference synthesis. Designed for single-GPU deployment in WeChat's large-scale consumer applications, the model processes text, reference images, and target latents as one interleaved sequence. A Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) backbone combines shared attention with independent understanding and generation parameters to limit optimization interference. Equipping each path with Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) modules provides sparse capacity, with 31.7B stored parameters and approximately 5.4B generation parameters activated per target latent token. A generation-oriented data engine combines a knowledge-grounded visual vocabulary with large-scale visual clustering to balance semantic coverage and editing tasks, while training-time evaluation guides iterative data refinement. Bilingual annotations and verified editing supervision support progressive training up to native 1.5K resolution. We optimize generation and editing separately with rubric- and checklist-based rewards, then consolidate the specialized policies through noise-aware on-policy distillation. In the reported overall comparisons, the 1536-resolution model ranks first among the evaluated open-source models on PRISM-Bench, Qwen-Image-Bench, and UnicBench. MeanFlow-based few-step distillation yields WeLM-Image-Turbo, which generates a 1024times1024 image in 4.98\,s on a single NVIDIA H20 GPU using eight guidance-free steps.
hf.title_ja: WeLM-Image：視覚的知能に向けた統一画像生成モデル
hf.summary_ja: 画像生成、編集、参照合成を1つのシーケンスとして処理し、MoE構造により高効率かつ単一GPUで動作可能なWeChat向けの基盤モデル。

hf.title: Factorized MLLM Embeddings for Composed Image Retrieval
hf.abstract: Composed Image Retrieval (CIR) aims to retrieve a target image given a reference image and a modification text. Although recent approaches leveraging Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have shown significant progress, we argue that the MLLM's compositional understanding remains underutilized. This stems from directly mapping composed queries into a retrieval embedding via contrastive supervision alone, without explicitly resolving the intended visual modifications. In this work, we introduce Factorized MLLM Embeddings (FactEmbed), which decouples compositional query comprehension from building discriminative embeddings. Rather than directly projecting the composed query into a single embedding without internal reasoning, FactEmbed employs a set of factorized latents that simulate the intended visual modifications via an intermediate target imagination objective. This process encourages the latents to ground into target semantics before forming discriminative representations for retrieval. Subsequently, to propagate these factorized representations throughout the model for retrieval, we optimize a factor-level contrastive loss while distilling the decomposed representations into a deeper attention layer of the MLLM. Finally, for efficient inference, we retain the [EOS] token to establish a global-level embedding on top of these factorized latents, while we exploit the mean-pooled factorized latents to rerank a short candidate list at negligible cost, as both are produced by the same forward pass. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that FactEmbed outperforms prior works across CIR benchmarks.
hf.title_ja: 構成的画像検索のための因子分解型MLLM埋め込み
hf.summary_ja: 画像と指示文を組み合わせた検索において、指示による変更意図を明示的に分解して抽出することで、MLLMの構成的理解を最大限に活用する。

hf.title: P^2-MOPD: Accelerating Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation via Parameter Priors
hf.abstract: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation consolidates expert capabilities by supervising student-generated trajectories, whereas task arithmetic offers a training-free alternative through linear parameter combinations. We view the linear combination of student and expert parameters as a single differentiable model and propose P^2-MOPD, which jointly optimizes the mixing coefficients and the student weights under the same on-policy distillation objective. Unlike task arithmetic, which stays within the span of the frozen student and expert parameters for any choice of merging coefficients, P^2-MOPD keeps the student trainable, so the experts act as parameter priors without confining it to this span. Across four domains at 1.7B and 4B scales, P^2-MOPD achieves faster and more balanced recovery than MOPD from the same initialization, surpassing its final average recovery in half the training steps. At the end of training, our 1.7B model reaches 94.7% average recovery, versus 80.9% for MOPD.
hf.title_ja: P^2-MOPD：パラメータプライアを介したマルチティーチャー・オンポリシー蒸留の加速
hf.summary_ja: 複数の専門家モデルの知見を学生モデルに統合する際、重みの線形結合を最適化に取り入れ、学習の効率と性能を向上させる手法を提案。

hf.title: TailSteer: Trajectory-Tail Steering for Drift-Resistant Multi-turn Image Editing
hf.abstract: Strong single-turn editing performance does not guarantee reliable multi-turn interaction: as edited outputs are repeatedly reused, small unintended changes can accumulate into severe visual drift. This long-term drift is often mitigated through training on multi-turn data or cross-turn rollouts, potentially altering pretrained priors, or through specialized inference-time mechanisms that are difficult to scale to foundation models. We introduce TailSteer, a final-stage training framework that improves multi-turn robustness while retaining the generative and editing capabilities acquired through earlier training. TailSteer follows a simple principle: keep early denoising dynamics close to those of the base model and concentrate preservation corrections near the trajectory tail, where fine-grained deviations can be suppressed. These corrections are learned from the editor's own on-policy denoising rollouts, using unchanged source content as a preservation reference without requiring curated ground-truth editing pairs. Experiments across the FLUX, SenseNova, and Qwen families show that TailSteer substantially reduces cumulative drift over 15-20 editing turns while largely preserving base-model performance on extensive text-to-image and single-image editing benchmarks. These results demonstrate that long-horizon editing robustness can be unlocked in foundation models after TailSteer, rather than by relearning their existing capabilities.
hf.title_ja: TailSteer：ドリフト耐性のあるマルチターン画像編集のための軌道末端ステアリング
hf.summary_ja: 複数回の画像編集で発生する画質の劣化（ドリフト）を防ぐため、ノイズ除去の初期段階を元画像に近づけるよう調整する学習フレームワーク。

hf.title: ToolSpace: Scaling Tool-Centric Environment Synthesis for Long-Horizon Agents
hf.abstract: Large language models are deployed as long-horizon agents that compose diverse tools across MCP services into executable workflows. Existing MCP environment-scaling methods are data-centric: they first synthesize a database and scenario, then derive tools and tasks from them. As a result, tool interfaces may not match real ones, tool compositions are not grounded in execution, and tasks rarely span more than one environment. We propose ToolSpace, a tool-centric framework that reverses this order. ToolSpace mines data, state, and retry dependencies from adjacent calls in execution traces of real MCP services and open agent corpora, using deterministic rules rather than LLM judgment, and clusters the resulting weighted tool-composition graph into environments. Databases are synthesized only for state-mutating environments, while query and stateless tools replay recorded returns. ToolSpace then performs state-aware random walks with rollback and decompiles each chain into a natural-language task with assertion-based checks, keeping only samples that replay successfully from the initial state. Applied to AutomationBench and tau3-Bench Banking, the pipeline produces harder Pro versions on which 7 frontier models drop by up to 38.2 points. Across seven long-horizon tool-use benchmarks, ToolSpace raises Qwen3.6-35B-A3B from 23.0 to 41.0 average score (43.2 with RL) and GLM-5.2 from 44.6 to 56.6, on par with Claude Opus 5. Ablations show that execution-witnessed edges clearly outperform LLM-judged ones, and performance keeps improving with data and environment scale.
hf.title_ja: ToolSpace：長期実行エージェントのためのツール中心の環境合成のスケールアップ
hf.summary_ja: 実際のサービス実行ログからツールの依存関係を抽出し、現実の仕様に即した複雑なマルチステップタスク環境を自動生成するフレームワーク。

hf.title: What Does Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning Really Improve in LLM Agents?
hf.abstract: While multi-turn agentic reinforcement learning (RL) excels on long-horizon tasks, its performance gains remain highly sensitive to interaction constraints. Evaluating across sampling breadth K and interaction depth T via Pass@(K,T), we show that trajectory-level RL advantages depend on sufficient turn budgets, diminishing significantly when budgets tighten. Besides, agentic RL does not uniformly elevate single-step decision quality; rather, its strength concentrates in error recovery and long-horizon resilience. To mitigate the deployment risks caused by this budget dependence, we provide a preliminary discussion on the benefits and limitations of process supervision signals and introduce BudgetMix RL as an alternative that varies interaction budgets during training. Experiments demonstrate that BudgetMix RL achieves robust performance across diverse execution settings. Project Page: https://rethinking-agentic-rl.github.io/
hf.org: Chinese Academic of Science Institute of Automation
hf.title_ja: マルチターン強化学習はLLMエージェントの何を改善するのか？
hf.summary_ja: 強化学習による性能向上は試行回数に依存し、単一の決定精度よりもエラー回復や長期的な回復力に寄与することを明らかにした調査報告。

hf.title: Open-HumanScale: An Open Recipe for Scaling Human and Robot Experience for Embodied Foundation Models
hf.abstract: Egocentric human video offers a scalable source of manipulation priors for robot learning, yet translating raw data scale into generalizable robot policies demands rigorous data curation and training recipes. We introduce Open-HumanScale, the first fully open recipe for scaling egocentric pretraining to 50,000 hours, anchored by Open-HumanScale-50K---a curated egocentric video corpus densely annotated with hand motion and natural language. Leveraging this corpus, we systematically investigate pure human pretraining via closed-loop simulation evaluations and uncover an empirical log-linear scaling law linking pretraining data hours to downstream robot success rates. Grounded in these findings, we develop HumanWAM-Vanilla, a world--action model pretrained exclusively on 50k hours of egocentric human video. Upon robot post-training, HumanWAM-Vanilla reaches 92.08% success on RoboTwin 2.0 Clean2Clean and 68.88% on Clean2Random, alongside a 14.17% mean success rate and a 19.00 mean progress score on RoboDojo. To push the capability frontier further, we explore joint human--robot pretraining with HumanWAM-Goal, a visual-goal-conditioned world--action model. Hybrid data scaling unlocks broad zero-shot generalization across both simulation and physical benchmarks, propelling post-trained RoboTwin 2.0 performance to new state-of-the-art levels: 92.70% on Clean2Clean and a substantial leap to 84.60% on Clean2Random. On physical robots, HumanWAM-Goal further exhibits emergent embodied in-context learning, dynamically adapting its manipulation behavior to unseen visual goals without parameter updates. To support reproducible scaling research in embodied AI, we open-source the Open-HumanScale-50K corpus, data curation and pretraining pipelines, alongside the pretrained and post-trained HumanWAM checkpoints, inference code, and simulation evaluation suites.
hf.title_ja: Open-HumanScale：身体性基盤モデルのための人間とロボットの経験を拡張するオープンレシピ
hf.summary_ja: 5万時間の主観視点映像データを公開し、人間の行動から学習する量とロボットの成功率にログ線形の相関があることを実証した学習手法。

hf.title: GameVerse: A Minute-Scale Gameplay Dataset for Long-Horizon Interactive World Modeling
hf.abstract: Recent advances in interactive world models have made it possible to generate controllable, dynamic environments from action inputs. Yet current models struggle to maintain coherence beyond roughly one minute of rollout, a limitation rooted not in model capacity but in the scarcity of long-horizon training data. Existing gameplay video datasets typically consist of clips under ten seconds, with captions that describe whole clips in coarse and undifferentiated text, which is insufficient for controllable long-horizon generation. We address this with GameVerse, a minute-scale gameplay video dataset purpose-built for long-horizon interactive world modeling. GameVerse contains 69.7K clips spanning 1,655 hours and 349.6 million frames across diverse first- and third-person gameplay, including 1,358 hours of continuous two-minute sequences, an order of magnitude longer than prior datasets. Clips pass through a unified pipeline of scene-consistent segmentation, quality filtering, camera pose estimation, and event-based caption annotation. Each clip is paired with a temporally stable camera trajectory that remains coherent across minutes, together with captions that separate static scene context from dynamic foreground events and align to event boundaries rather than fixed time windows. Comprehensive analysis shows that GameVerse surpasses existing public datasets in scale, diversity, and annotation quality. Experiments further demonstrate that training on GameVerse substantially extends the temporal horizon of interactive world models.
hf.title_ja: GameVerse：長期的な対話型世界モデルのための分単位ゲームプレイデータセット
hf.summary_ja: 1分を超える一貫した動画生成を可能にするため、詳細な説明が付与された長尺のゲームプレイ映像7万本を収録したデータセットを構築。

hf.title: EvoMemState: Evolving Memory State for Personal Agents
hf.abstract: Long-term memory enables large language model (LLM) agents to provide continuous personalized assistance by retaining user information across interactions. Existing systems support this process through fact extraction, organization, updating, and retrieval, but largely maintain memories as independent facts. This fact-centric paradigm may overlook how new facts update, constrain, or conflict with earlier ones, while leaving their applicability, role, and priority for the current request implicit. In this paper, we introduce EvoMemState, a state-centric framework that augments persistent facts with two complementary states: Relational States that capture how facts remain valid and relate to one another as memory evolves, and a Reasoning State that determines how these facts should be applied to the current request. Specifically, EvoMemState consists of three key components: (i) Ontology-Guided Memory State Induction extracts Persistent Facts and constructs Relational States that maintain their validity, scope, and evolving relations. (ii) RL-Based State Evolution internalizes memory-use experience into a policy through reinforcement learning to generate a request-specific Reasoning State. (iii) State-Aware Reasoning then combines the relevant facts with their Relational States and the generated Reasoning State to guide the personal agent. Extensive experiments on long-term dialogue and memory-use benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements over existing memory systems in retrieval completeness and memory-grounded response accuracy. Our code and implementation details are available at https://github.com/XMUDeepLIT/EvoMemState.git.
hf.title_ja: EvoMemState：個人用エージェントのための進化するメモリ状態
hf.summary_ja: 記憶を独立した事実として扱うのではなく、事実間の矛盾や優先度などの「関係性」と「重要度」の状態を動的に更新する記憶管理フレームワーク。

hf.title: PCBRouteAgent: How Close Are LLM Agents to Becoming PCB Routing Engineers?
hf.abstract: Automating printed circuit board (PCB) routing requires coordinating board-level connectivity decisions with geometric execution under strict design rules. Although recent agents can interact with native routing tools, reliable routing on complex boards remains challenging. We present PCBRouteAgent, a multimodal PCB routing agent inspired by how human engineers coordinate global strategy with local execution. A Global Routing Planner combines board images and structured electrical and geometric information to specify connection topology, routing order, corridors, and layer transitions. A Detailed Routing Executor realizes these guides through KiCad's native routing engine and performs bounded local recovery. Unresolved failures are returned as structured feedback, enabling targeted guide revisions while preserving accepted routes. We evaluate PCBRouteAgent on 247 synthetic and real-world boards from four PCBWorld-Bench test splits. It achieves clean-pass rates of 100%, 94.9%, 100%, and 40% on D2, D3-A, D3-B, and D3-C, respectively. On the three real-world subsets, PCBRouteAgent outperforms the best evaluated baseline in clean-pass rate by 13.9, 36, and 10 percentage points, respectively.
hf.title_ja: PCBRouteAgent：LLMエージェントはプリント基板設計エンジニアになれるか？
hf.summary_ja: 基板画像と電気情報を統合して全体戦略を立て、既存ツールを操作して局所的な配線を行う、人間の設計者の手順を模倣したマルチモーダルAI。

hf.title: Halley: A Predictive Control Plane for Optical AI Data Center Networks
hf.abstract: A frontier AI model is trained in an AI data center, on tens of thousands of accelerators joined by a dedicated network, and every training step ends with all of them exchanging data at once. Between racks, that network is optical, and each of its four layers, from lasers to switches, runs a fixed or after-the-fact policy. Lasers sharing an enclosure, cooling, and power can fail together. At a fixed spare ratio, correlated failure provably caps a pool's availability however large it grows. In this paper, we present a comprehensive predictive control plane framework, called Halley, that reads each resource's next state and acts before the failure occurs. It has four components, each carrying a formal guarantee: LightReserve that sizes the laser pool to provide a coverage bound, FoldFit that schedules the switch within 11/9 of the optimal, ThermaLead that holds a microring with one-step-ahead control, and TriageGuard that protects the highest-risk modules first. Halley gives each layer a predictive controller that defers to the deployed policy when unsure. Composed from simulations at that point, effective goodput, the share of ideal throughput kept, rises from 65.2\% to 76.5\% if a window that exhausts its spares is lost. If only the dark channels' bandwidth is lost, it reaches 67.4\%. Per megawatt, that is up to 1.03--1.17 times the training; for the same training, up to 3.3--14.7\% less data center capacity. Halley's fallback circuits are formally verified and are shown to achieve close timing on a commercial FPGA, and pass a 130~nm signoff.
hf.title_ja: Halley：光通信AIデータセンターネットワークのための予測制御プレーン
hf.summary_ja: 大規模AI学習時のネットワーク故障を防ぐため、資源の次状態を予測して故障発生前に先回りして制御を行う統合管理フレームワーク。

hf.title: VideoMemBench: How Well Do MLLMs Remember in Video Conversations?
hf.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can now process hour-long videos, making extended multi-turn dialogue over a single video a natural mode of use. Sustaining such a dialogue requires more than answering each question in isolation: the model must retrieve and reuse information established earlier in the conversation, both what it has seen and what it has said, an ability we term in-context video memory. Existing video QA benchmarks leave this ability unmeasured: their questions are mutually independent, never reference one another, and each is answerable from the video alone, so nothing ever requires carrying information across turns. We introduce VideoMemBench, in which each sample pairs a single video with a long multi-turn dialogue, whose turns are connected by typed cross-turn dependencies: an Episodic Dependency refers back to a visual episode described in an earlier turn, probing memory of what the model has seen, while an Answer Dependency builds on the model's own earlier answer, probing memory of what the model has said. Every dependency is verified considering two properties: 1) necessity, meaning the question cannot be answered without its earlier turns, and 2) non-leakage, meaning the question does not restate the information from its earlier turns. To enforce these properties, we design a construction pipeline with three LLM roles: a planner, a generator, and a judger, with each dialogue reviewed by human experts. VideoMemBench comprises 326 videos with 2,476 turns, of which 1,387 depend on earlier turns, including multi-parent dependencies and long-range call-back. Among over 20 evaluated open- and closed-source MLLMs, Claude Opus 5 performs the best with an overall score of only 45.7%, highlighting the challenge of in-context video memory. Our dataset and evaluation are released.
